results.title: Permuting conjugates and simplicity (Kourovka 10.66)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conjecture that a group $G$ containing nontrivial subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that the product set $AB$ is not all of $G$ and $A \cdot gBg^{-1} = gBg^{-1} \cdot A$ for every $g \in G$ is not simple. Products of subgroups are products of subsets of $G$.

results.title: A simple group with permuting conjugate subgroups (Kourovka 10.66 refuted)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a simple group $G$ and nontrivial subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ such that the product set $AB$ is not all of $G$ and $A \cdot gBg^{-1} = gBg^{-1} \cdot A$ for every $g \in G$, where products of subgroups are products of subsets of $G$. So the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 10.66 is false.

results.caption: Definition

results.title: The primes are dense in the coprime topology without 1
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: A nonempty set of primes is dense in the comaximal space iff it is infinite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Equip the positive integers with the comaximal topology, the topology generated by the sets $\{m : \gcd(n, m) = 1\}$ for positive integers $n$. A nonempty set $A$ of primes is infinite if and only if it is dense in this topology.

results.title: Coprime arithmetic progressions are dense in the comaximal space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Equip the positive integers with the comaximal topology, the topology generated by the sets $\{m : \gcd(n, m) = 1\}$ for positive integers $n$. results.title: Fourier–Laplace transform
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the Fourier–Laplace transform of $f$ at $z$ is the Lebesgue integral $\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, e^{-2\pi i x z} \, dx$, taken to be $0$ when the integrand is not integrable.

results.title: Fourier–Laplace transform on the real axis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real $r$, the Fourier–Laplace transform of $f$ at the complex number $r$, namely $\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, e^{-2\pi i x r} \, dx$, equals the Fourier transform of $f$ at $r$ with the $2\pi$ normalization, $\hat f(r) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{-2\pi i x r} f(x) \, dx$.

results.title: Derivative of the Fourier–Laplace transform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be integrable with compact support, and let $F(z) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, e^{-2\pi i x z} \, dx$ be its Fourier–Laplace transform. Then at every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, $F$ is complex differentiable with derivative $F'(z) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, (-2\pi i x) \, e^{-2\pi i x z} \, dx$.

results.title: The Fourier–Laplace transform of an integrable compactly supported function is entire
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be integrable with compact support. Then its Fourier–Laplace transform $z \mapsto \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, e^{-2\pi i x z} \, dx$ is complex differentiable at every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, that is, it is entire.

results.title: Turán system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers. A family $H$ of subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system when $0 < r < s \le n$, $H$ is $r$-uniform (every member of $H$ has exactly $r$ elements), and every $s$-element subset of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ contains some member of $H$.

results.title: Turán systems have positive uniformity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, whose definition includes $0 < r < s \le n$. Then $0 < r$.

results.title: A Turán system has $r < s$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then $r < s$.

results.title: A Turán system has $s \le n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then $s \le n$.

results.title: Turán systems are uniform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers. If $H$ is a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, then $H$ is $r$-uniform: every member of $H$ has exactly $r$ elements.

results.title: Turán systems cover every $s$-set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then every $s$-element subset $T$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ contains some member $e$ of $H$.

results.title: The complete $r$-graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $r$, the complete $r$-graph on $n$ vertices is the family of all $r$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: The complete $r$-graph is $r$-uniform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $r$, every member of the complete $r$-graph on $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ has exactly $r$ elements.

results.title: The complete $r$-graph is a Turán system
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$. Then the complete $r$-graph on $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ (the family of all its $r$-element subsets) is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system.

results.title: Realized sizes of Turán systems
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, the set of realized sizes is the set of natural numbers $k$ such that some Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has exactly $k$ members.

results.title: Membership in the realized sizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, $k$, the number $k$ lies in the set of realized sizes for $(n, s, r)$ if and only if some Turán $(n, s, r)$-system $H$ has exactly $k$ members.

results.title: Turán systems exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$ with $0 < r < s \le n$, there is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system.

results.title: Some size of a Turán system is realized
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$ with $0 < r < s \le n$, the set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$ is nonempty: some natural number $k$ is the number of members of a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$.

results.title: Turán number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, the Turán number $T(n, s, r)$ is the least element of the set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$, that is, the least number of members of a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, and $T(n, s, r) = 0$ if no such system exists.

results.title: The Turán number is a realized size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$ and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. Then $T(n, s, r)$ belongs to the set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$.

results.title: The Turán number is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$ and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. Then some Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$ has exactly $T(n, s, r)$ members.

results.title: Turán systems are at least as large as the Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. If $H$ is a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, then $T(n, s, r) \le |H|$.

results.title: Lower bounds on the Turán number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $s$, $r$, $b$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$. If $b \le k$ for every $k$ in the set of realized sizes for $(n, s, r)$ (the sizes of Turán $(n, s, r)$-systems), then $b$ is at most the Turán number $T(n, s, r)$.

results.title: Suffix of a list at an index
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $s = (s_0, \dots, s_{n-1})$ over a linearly ordered alphabet and a natural number $i$, the suffix of $s$ at $i$ is the list obtained from $s$ by dropping its first $i$ entries: it is $(s_i, \dots, s_{n-1})$ when $i < n$ and the empty list when $i \ge n$.

results.title: Suffixes of a list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $s$ of length $n$ over a linearly ordered alphabet, the list of suffixes of $s$ is the list, for $i = 0, 1, \dots, n$ in this order, of the lists obtained from $s$ by dropping its first $i$ entries. It starts with $s$ itself and ends with the empty list.

results.title: Suffix array
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $s$ of length $n$ over a linearly ordered alphabet, the suffix array of $s$ is the list of the indices $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, sorted so that the suffixes of $s$ starting at them appear in lexicographic order.

results.title: The suffix array is a permutation of the indices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a list $s$ of length $n$ over a linearly ordered alphabet, the suffix array of $s$ is a permutation of the list $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$ of all indices below $n$.

results.title: The suffix array sorts the suffixes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a list $s$ over a linearly ordered alphabet, the suffixes of $s$ taken in suffix-array order are sorted lexicographically: whenever an index $i$ comes before an index $j$ in the suffix array of $s$, the suffix of $s$ starting at $i$ is lexicographically less than or equal to the suffix of $s$ starting at $j$.

results.title: Longest common prefix length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For lists $x$ and $y$, $\mathrm{lcp}(x, y)$ is the length of the longest common prefix of $x$ and $y$: the number of positions, counted from the start, at which $x$ and $y$ agree before they first differ or one of them ends.

results.title: Two lists agree on their longest common prefix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $x$ and $y$ over a type with decidable equality, let $\operatorname{lcp}(x, y)$ be the length of their longest common prefix. Then the first $\operatorname{lcp}(x, y)$ elements of $x$ and the first $\operatorname{lcp}(x, y)$ elements of $y$ form the same list.

results.title: Common prefixes of every shorter length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be lists and let $\mathrm{lcp}(x, y)$ be the length of their longest common prefix. For every natural number $q \le \mathrm{lcp}(x, y)$, the first $q$ elements of $x$ and of $y$ agree.

results.title: Characterization of the longest common prefix length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $x$ and $y$, let $\mathrm{lcp}(x, y)$ be the length of the longest common prefix of $x$ and $y$. For every natural number $q$, we have $q \le \mathrm{lcp}(x, y)$ if and only if $q$ is at most the lengths of both $x$ and $y$ and the first $q$ elements of $x$ and of $y$ agree.

results.title: Longest-common-prefix lengths of adjacent suffixes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $s$ and a list of indices $i_0, i_1, \dots, i_k$, this is the list of length $k$ whose $t$-th entry, for $t < k$, is the length of the longest common prefix of the suffixes of $s$ starting at $i_t$ and at $i_{t+1}$, where the suffix starting at an index at or past the end of $s$ is the empty list. It has one entry per adjacent pair of indices, and it is empty for an empty index list.

results.title: The LCP array
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $s$ over a linearly ordered alphabet, the LCP array of $s$ is the list of longest-common-prefix lengths of adjacent suffixes in suffix-array order: if the suffix array of $s$ is $i_0, i_1, \dots, i_k$, then the LCP array has length $k$ and its $t$-th entry, for $t < k$, is the length of the longest common prefix of the suffixes of $s$ starting at $i_t$ and at $i_{t+1}$. It is empty when $s$ is empty.

results.title: Prefix classes are lexicographic intervals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `x ≤ y ≤ z` and `P` is a prefix of both `x` and `z`, then `P` is a prefix of `y`.

results.title: Truncation is monotone for the lexicographic order
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: The occurrences of a pattern are contiguous in the suffix array
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Binary search for the boundary of a predicate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Binary search for the boundary of a predicate on `[lo, hi)`: the first index at which `p` is false, assuming `p` holds on an initial segment of `[lo, hi)` (`lowerBound_spec`). Each call probes the midpoint and recurses on one half.

results.title: Number of probes made by the binary search

results.title: Binary search is correct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `p` holds on an initial segment of `[lo, hi)` (whenever it holds at `j`, it holds at every `i` with `lo ≤ i ≤ j`), then `lowerBound p lo hi` is the end `k` of that segment: `lo ≤ k ≤ hi`, `p` holds on `[lo, k)` and fails on `[k, hi)`.

results.title: Suffix-array search is correct

results.title: Ambient FK normalizer
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Probability of an ambient FK configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The probability of an ambient configuration: `fkWeight G p q ω / fkZ G p q`. For `0 < p < 1` and `q > 0`, its graph-edge marginal is the random-cluster law and unused coordinates are uniform.

results.title: Ambient random-cluster law as a probability mass function
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Agreement of configurations off an edge set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `ω` agrees with `ψ` on every edge outside `F`.

results.title: Fibre of configurations agreeing off an edge set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The fibre of configurations agreeing with `ψ` off `F`.

results.title: Total FK weight of a fibre
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total FK weight of the fibre `condFibre F ψ`.

results.title: FK measure induced on a fibre
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The FK measure induced on the fibre `condFibre F ψ`: FK weight divided by the fibre's total weight.

results.title: Random-cluster measure conditioned on the edges off a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The random-cluster measure conditioned on agreeing with `ψ` off `F`.

results.title: Domain Markov property (finite volume)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Conditioned on the states of the edges outside `F`, the random-cluster measure is the FK weight renormalized on the fibre (Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model*, 2006, Lemma 4.13).

results.title: Closing the edges of a set in a configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The configuration that closes every edge of `F` and agrees with `ψ` elsewhere.

results.title: Fibre representatives with every edge of a set closed

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Membership in `B` depends only on the states of edges outside `F`.

results.title: Toggling a non-edge leaves the open subgraph unchanged
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Off the edges of `G`, flipping `e` does not change the open subgraph.

results.title: Opening an edge does not increase the cluster count
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Opening an edge does not increase the number of clusters. This is a special case of Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent.card_le_card_of_le`, which proves it.

results.title: Opening an edge lowers the cluster count by at most one
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Opening an edge lowers the number of clusters by at most one.

results.title: Bernoulli product over the edges other than one edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Bernoulli product over the edges of `G` other than `e`.

results.title: Conditional probability that an edge is open given the rest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conditional probability under `φ_{G,p,q}` that `e` is open given the states of all other edges: `φ(setOpen e ω) / (φ(setOpen e ω) + φ(setClosed e ω))`.

results.title: Finite-energy constant of the random-cluster measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The finite-energy constant `min (p / (p + q (1 - p))) (1 - p)`.

results.title: Finite-energy property
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Finite-energy property of the random-cluster measure. For `p ∈ (0, 1)` and `q ≥ 1`, the conditional probability that an edge is open given all other edges lies in `[cFE p q, 1 - cFE p q]`. For edges of `G` the sharper bounds `p / (p + q (1 - p))` and `p` are proved along the way. See G. Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model* (2006), Chapter 3.

results.title: Inhomogeneous random-cluster weight

results.title: Partition function of the inhomogeneous random-cluster measure

results.title: Inhomogeneous Bernoulli product over all edges but one

results.title: Unnormalized inhomogeneous random-cluster expectation
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Differential formula
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Relabelling of an edge configuration by a vertex permutation
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Automorphism as an isomorphism of open subgraphs
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Boundary-preserving automorphisms preserve wired FK edge marginals

results.title: Isomorphic graphs have equal free FK probabilities after relabelling

results.title: Wired-graph isomorphism for a pulled-back configuration
results.caption: Definition
